topHiringRisks.title: Job Hopping & Stability Concerns
topHiringRisks.description: Multiple short stints (4-8 months) across different companies and domains suggest an inability to commit or see long-term product cycles through, which is critical for the sustained ownership and roadmap execution expected from a mid-level PM.

topHiringRisks.title: Level Mismatch & Experience Inflation
topHiringRisks.description: Despite strong individual project metrics, the actual tenure and 'Associate Product Manager' titles for the majority of the career suggest a junior-to-early-mid-level profile, not a solid mid-level expected for 3-5 years of stable, continuous experience. The '5+ years' claim is explicitly misleading.

topHiringRisks.title: Limited Broader Technical Depth for PM(T)
topHiringRisks.description: While strong in LLM/Prompt Engineering, the resume lacks explicit signals of deep technical tradeoff judgment, comprehensive system architecture understanding, or influencing complex engineering decisions beyond specific AI feature implementation, which is crucial for a 'Technical' PM.

rewriteExample.before: Re-architected VDB's unified inventory management system (VIMS) across web, ops, and warehouse teams by mapping high-friction workflow edge cases and consolidating fragmented data sources into a single source of truth, reducing inventory errors 30% across the VDB ecosystem.
rewriteExample.after: Led technical discovery and roadmap for a unified inventory management system (VIMS) by defining a normalized data model across fragmented legacy sources (SQL, NoSQL) and partnering with engineering to design RESTful APIs for real-time inventory sync, reducing data discrepancies and inventory errors by 30% across the VDB ecosystem.
rewriteExample.explanation: The 'after' version clarifies the PM's *technical* leadership (led technical discovery, defined data model, partnered on API design), specifies the underlying technical challenge/stack (SQL, NoSQL, RESTful APIs), and maintains the measurable outcome. This demonstrates stronger technical judgment and collaboration with engineering on system design, aligning better with 'technical fluency' and 'engineer trust' signals for a PM(T) role.
